newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM says army should stay out of politic.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM says army should stay out of politic.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said the country's army has been used by "power mongers" and that it should stay out of politics.

"The armed forces are the symbol of (a) nation's integrity and sovereignty. They should be kept out of all sorts of political controversy," Hasina told an army function in northern Mymensingh district on Sunday.
Hasina said her government was planning to involve the army in development work, the official BSS news agency said.
"There is a great potential in you as a disciplined and well-trained force...this potential has to be utilised in the development of the nation," she said. She did not elaborate.

Hasina, whose father and independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was killed in a 1975 army coup, expressed concern at what she said were "continued efforts by vested quarters to fuel controversy between (the) army and the government".
"Certain quarters are making false statements concerning the army and the Awami League government," Hasina said, without elaborating.
Hasina said the army had been used since 1975 for political reasons.
"The national army was used by ambitious power mongers. In a planned manner, conflict, controversy and indiscipline were created in army," she said.
Analysts said Hasina was referring to the opposition, particularly the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) which has its roots in the army, which she believes has tried to incite the army to revolt.
BNP leaders have been saying publicly that the government does not want the army to modernise because of its deep-seated anger over the killing of Hasina's father.
